target: UTM-bundled QEMU with HVF, virtio-ramfb, VirtIO keyboard/tablet, and WAV-backed VirtIO sound
command: QEMU=build/utm-qemu-probe/qemu-probe QEMU_VIRT='-L /Applications/UTM.app/Contents/Resources/qemu -machine virt,accel=hvf,gic-version=3 -cpu host -smp 1 -m 1024 -device virtio-ramfb -device virtio-keyboard-device -device virtio-tablet-device -audiodev wav,id=sound0,path=build/psalmody-heap-fix-utm-final.wav -device virtio-sound-pci,audiodev=sound0' ZEAL_COMPAT_LOG_PATH=build/check-psalmody-heap-fix-utm-final.log python3 -u scripts/check-compat.py --pci --quick --probe-psalmody --probe-psalmody-audio-timer
verified: The stock editor remained visible through redraw-aware scans, accepted recording and H-key C5 note entry, and entered playback.
WAV capture contains C5 in three consecutive 50 ms windows.
Shift+Escape exited playback; the graphical terminal evaluated 40+2 as 42 and zstatus reported failed=0.
The experimental audio timer delivered 10 IRQs.
limits: Automated UTM-bundled QEMU and WAV evidence; it does not verify audible output in the live UTM application. The user previously reported hearing a Psalmody note and Oh Great through Pi 4B HDMI, but the exact Pi card image provenance was not verified.
